content: Phenobarbital reduces the levels of axitinib by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid or use alternative drugs with minimal CYP3A4 induction potential. Phenobarbital and azelastine both increase sedation. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Phenobarbital and baclofen both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. This increased metabolism may lead to reduced bazedoxifene exposure, potentially increasing the risk of endometrial hyperplasia. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or effects of bedaquiline by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers due to the risk of reduced therapeutic efficacy. Phenobarbital and belladonna/opium both increase sedation. Belladonna alkaloids also reduce cholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of belumosudil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider increasing the belumosudil dosage to 200 mg PO BID when coadministered with strong CYP3A inducers. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital increases the metabolism of bemiparin, reducing its effects. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Phenobarbital and benazepril may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially leading to increased hypotensive effects. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of bendamustine by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism, potentially increasing the concentrations of active metabolites. Use caution and monitor closely. Benperidol increases the effects of belladonna alkaloids through pharmacodynamic synergy, while belladonna alkaloids reduce benperidol levels via pharmacodynamic antagonism and inhibition of GI absorption. Phenobarbital and benperidol both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death may occur if coadministered. Avoid or use alternative drugs unless no other treatment options are available. Limit dosages and durations to the minimum required. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while benzphetamine decreases sedation. The interaction effect is unclear. Use caution and monitor closely. Belladonna alkaloids and benztropine both reduce cholinergic effects, potentially leading to additive anticholinergic adverse effects. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of berotralstat by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of betaxolol by increasing metabolism. Consider a higher beta-blocker dose during coadministration. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected. Monitor closely. Bethanechol increases cholinergic effects, while belladonna alkaloids decrease them. The interaction effect is unclear. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of bexagliflozin, a UGT1A9 substrate. Consider adding another antihyperglycemic agent for additional glycemic control. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of bexarotene by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of bictegravir by inducing CYP3A4 and UGT1A1 metabolism, potentially leading to therapeutic failure and resistance. Avoid coadministration with strong inducers. Consider alternative anticonvulsants. Phenobarbital reduces biotin levels through an unspecified mechanism. Biotin supplementation may be necessary. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of bisoprolol by increasing metabolism. Consider a higher beta-blocker dose during coadministration. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital increases the metabolism of bivalirudin, reducing its effects. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Blinatumomab increases phenobarbital levels by reducing metabolism, particularly during the first 9 days of the first cycle and the first 2 days of the second cycle. Monitor closely for drug-drug interactions, especially with narrow therapeutic index CYP450 substrates. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of bortezomib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of bosentan by inducing CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of bosutinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, decreasing plasma concentrations by approximately 85%. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Bremelanotide may reduce phenobarbital absorption by slowing gastric emptying. Avoid coadministration with oral drugs dependent on threshold concentrations for efficacy. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of brentuximab vedotin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital and brexanolone both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of brexpiprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Double the brexpiprazole dose over 1–2 weeks if coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of brigatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially decreasing efficacy. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Phenobarbital and brimonidine both increase sedation. Increased CNS depression may occur. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital and brinzolamide may increase the risk of anticonvulsant-induced osteomalacia through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of brivaracetam by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Both drugs increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Brodalumab may normalize CYP450 enzyme formation by reducing cytokine levels during chronic inflammation. Monitor therapeutic effects when initiating or discontinuing brodalumab in patients on narrow therapeutic index CYP450 substrates. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of bromocriptine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital and brompheniramine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of budesonide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital and bupivacaine implant may increase the risk of methemoglobinemia. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of buprenorphine (all forms) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase sedation. Monitor closely for withdrawal symptoms or consider alternative treatment options. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of bupropion by increasing metabolism. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of buspirone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital and butabarbital both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital and butalbital both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital and butorphanol both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of cabazitaxel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of cabotegravir by inducing UGT1A1 and UGT1A9 metabolism, increasing the risk of virologic failure. Coadministration is contraindicated. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of cabozantinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. If necessary, adjust the cabozantinib dose and monitor closely. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while caffeine decreases sedation. The interaction effect is unclear. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces caffeine levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of calcifediol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, shortening its half-life. Monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces the levels of calcitriol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital and calcium/magnesium/potassium/sodium oxybates increase each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. Coadministration is contraindicated.
